item.title: Stellar Blade: BLOOD RAIN teases me with some R&B—and I'm here for it
item.description: But the studio's stance about its underaged, oversexualized protagonist is very much still making me uncomfortable.
item.dc:creator: Peterline6
item.content:encoded:
I find myself in a bit of a tough spot regarding Stellar Blade, and even more so with its sequel, BLOOD RAIN, teased via a provocative trailer last June. We're introduced to Evie, a (very) young member of an anti-terrorist unit in a futuristic city inspired by Chongqing, China. My discomfort stems from the fact that the trailer raised some very legitimate questions regarding the protagonist's juvenile appearance, showcased in an excessively tight outfit and highlighted by voyeuristic camera angles. The game's director has waved away the critics, insisting that the heroine's personality will outweigh her appearance... all while promising outfits even more "appealing" than those in Stellar Blade. Coming from the studio behind Goddess of Victory: NIKKE, should we even be surprised?

That said, it is with a healthy dose of caution that I invite you to check out the first two tracks of the "Summer Game Fest EP" shared yesterday by SHIFT UP. Composed by Youngjee Lee—who was already heavily involved in the massive soundtrack of the first game—these pieces showcase two very different sides of the BLOOD RAIN atmosphere. The first, "Make up my mind," is an absolute R&B/soul delight that hits my feels perfectly thanks to its relentless groove and the singer's sustained vocals. "Off the line," on the other hand, shifts gears completely from the Stellar Blade OST by leaning into a heavy rock sound flirting with Drum and Bass—an epic track that makes you imagine yourself slicing through enemies in the heat of battle.

Ultimately, everyone is free to take Stellar Blade: BLOOD RAIN however they like. The original game's soundtrack remains an anomaly in the industry—boasting over 200 tracks and 10+ hours of music. Earlier this year, the British label Laced Records opened pre-orders for a vinyl edition. A release that is criticized by fans for its meager tracklist—only 44 tracks were selected, following what I imagine was a hell of a curation headache.

item.title: Ben Starr stans, assemble: a new Soulframe track features your favorite voice
item.description: Take a listen to Verso's verse.
item.dc:creator: Peterline6
item.content:encoded:
Digital Extremes—the studio behind Warframe—is cranking out progress on their fantasy action RPG, and the latest updates from TennoCon have the fanbase cheering. While the game is already accessible in alpha for those who grabbed a founder's pack, the studio has already begun teasing the vibe with various musical snippets. Today, a new track joins the jukebox: "Silver Eyes," first revealed on the "Warsongs" trailer, performed by singer Lorelei Marcell and featuring a guest verse from voice actor Ben Starr. The single is now playing on all streaming platforms.

Starr is a household name in the industry, having voiced main characters in Final Fantasy XVI and Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. In Soulframe, he’s set to play the primary antagonist, Tempest Bayor. It’s a powerhouse cast, especially with Jennifer English (Clair Obscur, Baldur's Gate 3) joining the lineup recently. Those two really are inseparable, eh?

You can head over to the official Soulframe page to check out the roadmap, though it looks like we won’t be seeing a full 1.0 release for a long, long time.

item.title: Make yourself at home : the World of Warcraft housing soundtrack has arrived
item.description: Keep thinking about your character's home during your daily commute.
item.dc:creator: Peterline6
item.content:encoded:
Finally introduced in World of Warcraft for the latest expansion, Midnight, the famous MMORPG’s housing system allows anyone to acquire a plot of land and decorate it to their liking. It’s essentially a game within a game, featuring its own mechanics and, naturally, a bespoke soundtrack.

Blizzard Entertainment has reunited with its favorite composers—notably David Arkenstone, a veteran of the game’s tavern music—to provide this alternative game mode with a relaxing yet rigorously authentic Azerothian soundscape. You can expect to hear motifs and instruments that evoke the game's various factions and environments, all wrapped in a cozy atmosphere designed to let you take your time perfecting your interior design.

Full soundtracks for World of Warcraft and other Blizzard titles are available on streaming platforms as well as for purchase on Bandcamp. For those following my previous piece on naming conventions for video game OSTs, you'll note that the American studio has once again shifted its naming style with this latest album.

Related
Why nobody can agree on what to call video game music Despite the roughly 1,200 soundtracks released every year on streaming platforms, there doesn't seem to be a fixed convention for album naming.

item.title: UNBEATABLE’s high-voltage post-punk soundtrack finally hits streaming
item.description: UNBEATABLE hits Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer and more
item.dc:creator: Peterline6
item.content:encoded:
The rhythm game/visual novel from D-CELL Games is making waves. Alongside news of a vinyl release at iam8bit and a fresh DLC (complete with its own Bandcamp soundtrack), the high-octane post-punk OST of UNBEATABLE has officially landed on Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, Tidal, Deezer, and Qobuz. You can find all the links above. Note that it's still really fresh, and that you may have to wait a couple of hours for the rollout to be completed on your favorite streaming service.

In line with the studio's Steam announcements, the album featuring the diegetic tracks—performed by the game's own characters—is now available outside of Bandcamp. A second album, dubbed [ost], is expected in the coming days; this one serves as the game's actual score, providing the music for narrative beats and the atmospheric backdrop for the adventure's progression. While not yet official, it’s a safe bet that the recently released BREAKOUT and the newcomer The Jamie Paige Content Companion's Official Companion Content will also land on streaming platforms at some point.

As the studio reminded fans in their Steam post, "Of course, the best way you can support the SOUND TEAM and ensure we're able to continue making more tracks for the game is to purchase the soundtrack directly." I can’t stress this enough: streaming is convenient, but it doesn’t put food on the artists' tables. Buy the music you love!

UNBEATABLE is available on PC and, as of today, on Switch 2.

item.title: The Wolverine's first single is a gritty introduction to Logan
item.description: The soundtrack is composed by David Flemming, who recently scored Superman.
item.dc:creator: Peterline6
item.content:encoded:
San Diego Comic-Con has delivered its usual haul of juicy intel on Insomniac's next project, Marvel's Wolverine. Still slated for a September 15 release, this high-octane action game is getting a soundtrack from David Flemming—the composer who recently made waves with the score for the Superman film and the hit Apple TV series Widows Bay.

The first preview, aptly titled "Logan," serves as a compelling statement of intent for the game's musical direction. You can add it to your streaming platforms right now.

Clocking in at over six minutes, this long track acts as a sweeping introduction to the protagonist, shifting through several movements to showcase the various facets of his personality. For me, it’s a first taste that leaves you craving more, especially after (and this is a personal take) the somewhat "safe" scores by John Paesano for Marvel's Spider-Man and its sequel.

Moving away from the more open structure of the Spider-Man titles, Wolverine leans heavily into the gory, visceral nature of its combat. Speaking of which, Sony shared a new gameplay sequence during SDCC that is absolutely drenched in hemoglobin. You can check it out here.

item.title: Mahou Arms finally hits 1.0, and Dale North’s full OST is a vibe
item.description: Featuring the exquisite voice of Pernelle.
item.dc:creator: Peterline6
item.content:encoded:
After six long years in the early access trenches, Dischan Media’s action game is finally entering its 1.0 era. While the community has been steadily warming to it throughout development, Mahou Arms makes its mark by blending a heavy anime aesthetic with gameplay vibes reminiscent of NieR: Automata. To celebrate the official launch, composer Dale North teamed up with singer Pernelle (known for Stellar Blade and NIKKE) to deliver a high-octane opening cinematic. You can check it out below.

But the hype doesn't stop there: the full soundtrack, boasting 21 tracks, has officially landed on all streaming platforms. It’s a polished piece of work that feels deeply "J-RPG"—balancing sublime orchestration with electronic textures that perfectly drive the heroine through her combat sequences. It’s a fitting evolution for North, who first put himself on the map with the Wizard of Legend OST back in 2018.

On a side note: if Pernelle’s vocals have your name written all over them, you’ll want to check out her first EP with her band Paon. It sounds like a lost soundtrack from a Persona game that never actually made it to the shelves.

item.title: Award-winning Gordy Haab drops the first single for Star Wars Zero Company
item.description: The whole soundtrack will be released on August 27th.
item.dc:creator: Peterline6
item.content:encoded:
XCOM and Star Wars fans will have to sit tight for one more month before diving into this new tactical action game from Bit Reactor—a studio founded in 2022 under the leadership of Greg Foertsch, former art director at Firaxis Games (Civilization, XCOM...). Safe to say this team knows what they're doing, making a natural pair with EA's go-to Star Wars veteran, composer Gordy Haab.

Grammy winner for the score of Star Wars Jedi: Survivor, along with numerous other accolades for his work on Star Wars: Battlefront II and Indiana Jones and the Great Circle, Haab brings us the very first, self-titled track from the Zero Company soundtrack. Clocking in at just 1:17, this brief piece sets the tone for this tactical game set during the Clone Wars, complete with a motif that fans will easily recognize. The track is also available on your favorite streaming platform.

It's now official: the full OST will drop alongside the game on August 27. Star Wars Zero Company is heading to PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

item.title: Bargain with fate with the Schrödinger's Call soundtrack
item.description: The hit visual novel finally lets you enjoy its soundtrack on various streaming platforms.
item.dc:creator: Peterline6
item.content:encoded:
Unless you're deep into visual novels, you might not have heard of it yet, but Schrödinger's Call currently stands as the 4th highest-rated game of 2026, sitting ahead of titles like Pokopia and Resident Evil Requiem.

In this narrative adventure, you play as Mary, "the world's last confidant," who sits right on the threshold between life and death. Her goal is to bring a semblance of peace to her fellow souls by listening to their grief and regrets—even if it means bending a few rules along the way. While the game's fascinating story is occasionally weighed down by somewhat tedious design choices, it truly shines through its striking art style and, of course, the score by Seishi Irimajiri.

The Japanese composer delivers a generous 76-track album—mostly short pieces—that blends seamlessly with the game's Tim Burton-esque aesthetic and German expressionist vibes. You can stream it right now on Spotify, Apple Music, and other major platforms, or support the studio directly by grabbing a copy on Steam. Schrödinger's Call is also available on Nintendo Switch.

item.title: Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy is already bound to vinyl via Black Screen Records
item.description: Olivier Derivière partners up with the german label once more for a gorgeous physical release.
item.dc:creator: Peterline6
item.content:encoded:
The new entry in Asobo’s franchise isn't even out yet, but its musical roll-out is already locked in. Just like with all his previous soundtracks, composer Olivier Derivière (Streets of Rage 4, South of Midnight) is teaming up with German label Black Screen Records for a gorgeous 2LP release for Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy. The game is set to launch on PC and consoles on August 27, with the vinyl following in November. It’s available for €45 as a signed edition by the composer. In the US, Very Ok Vinyl will handle distribution for $47.

Marketing for this spin-off centered on the character of Sofia is picking up speed with just a few weeks left before launch. Alongside plenty of gameplay footage, we’ve already gotten a taste of three tracks from the OST of A Plague Tale Legacy, which takes a very different direction from the series' first two installments. Olivier Derivière teamed up with the Amalgamation Choir—a 20-woman choir led by Vasiliki Anastasiou—to ground the game’s score in the Cretan setting of Sofia’s journey.

I’ll take this opportunity to remind you that the vinyl soundtracks for A Plague Tale: Innocence and A Plague Tale: Requiem are still available on Black Screen Records’ website.

item.title: The Esoteric Ebb soundtrack is now finally complete — stream it now on Spotify, Apple Music and more
item.description: Volume 2 just dropped to kickstart the weekend.
item.dc:creator: Peterline6
item.content:encoded:
As promised to Bandcamp supporters by the composing trio, the second installment of the soundtrack for the fantasy CRPG Esoteric Ebb is now available worldwide. Rather than releasing it separately, the artists have combined both volumes into a single album, available on Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, Deezer, Tidal, and Qobuz.

A deeply atmospheric soundtrack, driven by delightful woodwinds, clean reverb-soaked guitar, and even a new feature with singer MØ, who lends her vocals to the track "Revel in Urth". The Danish singer previously appeared on several tracks from the first volume, which you can still listen to via the link above.

The 500-unit vinyl press of the Esoteric Ebb soundtrack is still available for pre-order on Bandcamp. Keep in mind that this 2LP set only includes tracks from the first volume — the artists haven't announced a potential second vinyl for collectors just yet.

item.title: Dutch DJ Daniel Wanrooy turns HypnoTiles into a worthy Tetris Effect successor
item.description: A short but striking EDM soundtrack.
item.dc:creator: Peterline6
item.content:encoded:
It's a big day for electronic music. Following the release of the ChainDive OST, we're turning our attention to an even lesser-known title: HypnoTiles. Released last month on PC, this Tetris offspring flew completely under the radar... but trust me, giving its soundtrack a listen might just convince you to check it out.

Composed by Dutch DJ Daniel Wanrooy (known for remixing Tiësto, Armin van Buuren, and other EDM legends), the HypnoTiles original soundtrack doesn't pull any punches. True to the game's name, it throws you into a near-hypnotic state of trance. Heart-pounding bass, melodic synths, and eerie pads are just some of the ingredients the producer uses to put you in an altered state.

Senile Team's inspiration for their game is pretty obvious: Tetris Effect. Even if HypnoTiles doesn't go quite as far or look quite as polished as its role model, the puzzle game relies on synesthesia to literally mesmerize its players. If you're a fan of Hydelic's musical work, the HypnoTiles soundtrack is very likely to strike a chord.

item.title: The cult techno soundtrack of ChainDive finally hits streaming
item.description: Over 20 years later, this banger OST finally shines on Spotify, Apple Music and more.
item.dc:creator: Peterline6
item.content:encoded:
As announced by its main composer, Yuji "TECHNOuchi" Takenouchi, on his social media, the original soundtrack for the PS2 game ChainDive and its official arrangement album have finally arrived on Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer and the likes. The album was originally published in 2022 on CD and Bandcamp.

Ranked among the top 10 PS2 game OSTs by DJ Dedeco (who sampled the soundtrack extensively for his mixes), ChainDive is a lesser-known title in Sony's catalog. Released exclusively in Japan and developed by the studio Alvion, it is an action side-scroller where you play as a sharp-bladed mecha ridding the planet of a monstrous invasion. The gameplay is exhilarating, but the soundtrack, which mixes techno and house music, is even more so.

Composed mainly by TECHNOuchi (Metal Gear Solid 2: Solid Snake, Circadia) and Hideyuki Eto (Armored Core series), the ChainDive original soundtrack has vastly outgrown the popularity of the game itself, and even 23 years later, it hasn't lost any of its club-worthy appeal. It sits way up here, just beside the legendary Ghost in the Shell PS1 soundtrack.

item.title: iam8bit announces the Mina the Hollower 3LP vinyl
item.dc:creator: Peterline6
item.content:encoded:
It was only a matter of time before the announcement dropped: just days after a teaser left no room for doubt, the American label iam8bit has officially opened pre-orders for a stunning 3LP vinyl soundtrack to Yacht Club Games' latest smash hit, Mina the Hollower. It'll set you back $64.99, with shipping scheduled for Q4 2026. In Europe, distribution is handled as usual by Germany's Black Screen Records, where it’s listed at €68.

Composed by Jake Kaufman—a composer who built a rock-solid reputation on the chiptune scene thanks to his work on Shovel Knight—the soundtrack to Mina the Hollower fits the Game Boy aesthetic of this deliciously retro Zelda-like like a glove. More about it right here.

Mina the Hollower’s old-school soul is alive and well in its stellar soundtrack. Composers Jake Kaufman and Yuzo Koshiro cooked up a chiptune-tastic feast using some pretty OG hardware; the original Game Boy sound chip, with just a sprinkling of the Konami Sound Cartridge (from the MSX) added to taste. 

The result is one of the best soundtracks of the year, video game or otherwise. Equal parts creepy and cozy, the music of Mina sets the perfect mood for its brilliantly-realized gothic world. 

iam8bit is proud to partner with the fine folks at Yacht Club Games to bring Mina’s soundtrack to life with a very special release. This is the Mina the Hollower 3xLP, pressed on rich, gorgeous Velvet Purple Splatter Vinyl. 

For the album artwork, we once again turned to Mina’s retro roots for inspiration. The center labels feature a zoetrope-inspired design with Mina herself in action, a celebration of Yacht Club’s devotion to the craft of pixel art and animation. The jacket, with art from our friend Nimit Malavia, boasts 3D-enhanced details — and in the spirit of everything throwback, we’ve included special Mina-themed 3D glasses that actually work with the artwork! The result is a release that feels like a truly unique piece of video game history. 

-- iam8bit

On top of the vinyl, iam8bit is also offering a keychain set and a notebook featuring artwork from the game. The entire collection is available at this address (as well as in Europe via Black Screen Records).

A few weeks ago, iam8bit also announced pre-orders for the vinyl and CD editions of the indie title Unbeatable.

item.title: Splatoon Raiders debuts on Nintendo Music
item.description:
Just in time for its Switch 2 exclusivity debut, Nintendo has shaken up its usual schedule to host nine previews of the Splatoon Raiders soundtrack. You can stream them right now on Nintendo Music (requires a Nintendo Switch Online subscription).

Staying true to the franchise’s lineage, the Splatoon
item.dc:creator: Peterline6
item.content:encoded:
Just in time for its Switch 2 exclusivity debut, Nintendo has shaken up its usual schedule to host nine previews of the Splatoon Raiders soundtrack. You can stream them right now on Nintendo Music (requires a Nintendo Switch Online subscription).

Staying true to the franchise’s lineage, the Splatoon Raiders music reeks of hot sand, palm trees, and sun-tanned skin. These first snippets are relatively chill—even if they still carry that signature musical quirkiness that defines this "not-your-average" TPS. 

While we're still waiting on the official word regarding the composers, let’s assume Nintendo has once again tapped the same crew that handled Splatoon 3: Shiho Fujii, Masato Ohashi, Kairi Hamada, Yumi Takahashi, Toshiyuki Sudo, Asuka Hayazaki, Toru Minegishi, and Ryo Nagamatsu (the latter of whom puts his name on this year’s best OST, Denshattack!).

Last week, Nintendo also highlighted one of the most critically acclaimed titles of its catalog, releasing the insanely packed soundtrack of Donkey Kong Bananza on its streaming platform.

Splatoon Raiders is available today as a Switch 2 exclusive.
